newsitem.title: UK: ICCO puts world 96/97 cocoa deficit at 115,000 T.
newsitem.headline: ICCO puts world 96/97 cocoa deficit at 115,000 T.

text.p: The International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) said on Thursday the world's 1996/97 cocoa production deficit should be about 115,000 tonnes.
That compares with last year's surplus of 160,000 tonnes.
To get that total, ICCO revised up its world cocoa bean production forecast by 93,000 tonnes to 2.715 million tonnes compared with its forecast in December 1996.
It also revised its 1996/97 world cocoa grindings estimate down to 2.803 million tonnes. That is 18,000-tonnes lower than its December 1996 estimate.

ICCO said its overall upward revision to 1996/97 world cocoa bean production resulted from upward adjustments made only for the African region. It now forecasts production in the African region at 1.761 million tonnes, up 139,000 tonnes.

Larger-than-expected crops are expected from Ivory Coast, Nigeria and Ghana. Ivory Coast's crop forecast was seen up 125,000 tonnes at 1.125 million tonnes, Nigeria up 10,000 tonnes at 150,000 and Ghana up 5,000 tonnes at 335,000.
Production in the Americas was expected to drop 34,000 tonnes to 457,000 and Asia and Oceania production was seen falling 12,000 tonnes to 497,000.
Brazil's production was expected to fall 30,000 tonnes to 165,000 tonnes, Indonesia down 5,000 tonnes to 325,000 and Malaysia down 5,000 to 115,000 tonnes.
Those world cocoa production figures compare with the ICCO's 1995/96 revision to 2.918 million tonnes, up 18,000 tonnes from the figure in its last Quarterly Bulletin.
The 1995/96 revision reflects higher than expected production in Malaysia by 10,000 tonnes, Nigeria by 8,000 tonnes and Indonesia by 5,000.
But Mexico's 1995/96 production was revised down 4,000 tonnes.
World cocoa bean grindings in 1996/97 were revised down 18,000 tonnes but were still seen posting a record high 2.803 million tonnes.
ICCO revised down 1996/97 grindings estimates for Western Europe and Asia and Oceania to reflect lower forecasts for Germany, the UK, France and Indonesia.
German grindings were seen dropping 10,000 tonnes to 255,000 tonnes, the UK down 10,000 to 180,000, France down 5,000 to 120,000 and Indonesia down 5,000 to 70,000 tonnes.
But 1996/97 grinding forecasts were raised for the Americas. U.S. grindings were seen gaining 5,000 tonnes to 365,000 tonnes with Brazil up 5,000 to 190,000 tonnes.
Eastern European and African 1996/97 grindings estimates remained at 172,500 and 283,000 tonnes, respectively.
Those estimates compare with ICCO's 1995/96 world grinding figure of 2.279 million tonnes, down 9,000 tonnes from its last Quarterly Bulletin.
For 1995/96 the ICCO now saw France's grindings down 7,000 tonnes and Malaysia's down 5,000.
But Ireland's grindings were seen up 3,000 tonnes in 1995/96.
With the 1996/97 deficit projected at 115,000 tonnes, total statistical cocoa bean stocks at the end of the season should decline to 1.271 million tonnes.

Excluding ICCO buffer stock holdings of 26,000 tonnes at the end of the 1996/97 year, total stocks directly overhanging the market would amount to 1.245 million tonnes, or above five months of estimated annual world grindings in 1996/97.
--Medora Lee, London newsroom +44 171 542 8072
